teaser.text: MetLife sells protection and long-term payment promises, then invests the money it receives to help meet them. Its business ranges from workplace benefits to pension transfers and institutional investment management.

stock.title: MetLife stock forecast
stock.meta_description: MetLife stock forecast covering weighted scenarios, operating drivers, cash returned to shareholders and valuation.
stock.opening: MetLife's weighted path is $113.98 in October 2029, or +21%. It hinges on earnings enduring.
stock.closing: The full MetLife memo also explains its business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could MetLife's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: MetLife’s weighted path is modestly positive: $98.82 in October 2027, or +1%, and $113.98 in October 2029, or +21%, provided earnings endure, parent liquidity remains adequate and new business is priced for risk. New Frontier targets adjusted ROE of 15%–17% through 2029 and a 100-basis-point reduction in the direct expense ratio. Management also targets $25.0 billion of company free cash flow through 2029 to support debt service, acquisitions, dividends, repurchases and a safety buffer. The forecast assigns 25% to the bear case, 55% to the base case and 20% to the bull case, with October 2029 prices ranging from $44.33 to $192.89. The November 5, 2026 results call will test earnings growth and expense control after PineBridge. RIS liability growth, Group Benefits renewals, PineBridge’s contribution, third-party MIM flows and constant-currency international results will determine whether growth becomes durable earnings. The thesis is a modest gain backed by execution, liquidity and disciplined risk pricing.

The range is much wider than the weighted path suggests. The bear case reaches $44.33 by October 2029. The bull case reaches $192.89. The probabilities are 25% for bear, 55% for base and 20% for bull.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for MetLife, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The bull would require stronger employer retention, controlled claims and attractive PRT returns. Persistent PineBridge clients, rising third-party flows and earnings that support larger buybacks would justify the higher multiple.

blocks.heading: How much cash does MetLife really make?

paragraphs.text: The share count moves with buybacks, stock compensation and new share sales. MetLife’s year-end shares fell from 825.5 million in 2021 to 655.3 million in 2025, while buybacks exceeded stock-based pay throughout that period.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for MetLife today?

paragraphs.text: MetLife, Inc. is the holding company above its insurance and asset-management businesses. The price-to-earnings, or P/E, ratio tells investors how much they pay for each dollar of annual earnings. MetLife’s reported, core and forward P/Es differ sharply, which means the stock looks far more expensive on recent reported earnings than on adjusted or expected earnings.

blocks.heading: How much does MetLife pay its shareholders per share?

paragraphs.text: The base dividend rises from $2.49 to $2.97 per share. The bear case holds it at $2.37, the latest annualized rate, while the bull case reaches $3.32. The five-year record shows increases from $1.90 to $2.25, but no explicit dividend-growth target exists.

blocks.heading: Is MetLife's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: The parent company mainly receives usable cash through dividends from its regulated subsidiaries, and regulators can restrict those payments. That is why reported earnings, parent cash, reserves, liquidity and debt must be considered together before judging a buyback or acquisition.
**Paid out, % of earnings for common** — Excluding the $982 million asset-transfer loss, 2023 dividends and buybacks consumed 197.7% of common earnings, compared with 338.3% reported.

paragraphs.text: The view would move toward bear if private-equity returns, variable investment income or credit experience weaken during 2027–2029. Adverse claims or underpriced pension transfers would pressure RIS earnings. Tighter subsidiary remittances or integration costs would reduce parent cash and buybacks.

earnings.meta_description: MetLife reports next on November 4, 2026; guidance, results and PineBridge integration are the key watchpoints.
earnings.opening: The next MetLife results are expected on November 4, 2026. Watch whether adjusted earnings growth and expense control continue after the PineBridge addition.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers questions about the business of MetLife, its rivals, its management and its risks.

blocks.heading: What has MetLife guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Management’s promise is a set of operating gauges, not a promise of one GAAP profit number. GAAP is the standard accounting rulebook; adjusted earnings remove items MetLife considers unusually volatile or less useful for judging ongoing operations, such as investment gains, derivative effects and certain acquisition costs. Adjusted return on equity, or ROE, measures adjusted profit against shareholder capital, while the direct expense ratio compares direct costs with the revenue base.

blocks.heading: Has MetLife kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: MetLife also reports an encouraging first year under New Frontier. In 2025, adjusted earnings per share grew by double digits, adjusted ROE reached 16%, and the direct expense ratio was 11.7%, within or better than the stated targets. The company also says it exceeded every commitment in its previous strategy.

blocks.heading: What do MetLife’s last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: MetLife reported adjusted-earnings growth across its operating segments, supported by favorable underwriting and volume growth. Adjusted premiums, fees and other revenues excluding PRT also grew. That breadth matters because improvement in one product can be temporary, while progress across several businesses is more informative.

Reported investment income rose 18% in Q2 2026. Adjusted investment income rose 7%, because fair-value movements affected the reported figure. MetLife also recorded an impairment related to a planned Ukraine disposal and real-estate impairments during the first half. Those charges do not erase operating progress, but they make reported net income a poor figure to annualize.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in MetLife’s next results?

paragraphs.text: MetLife’s scheduled November 5 results call will test whether adjusted earnings growth and expense control continue after the PineBridge addition. A beat alone will not settle the question; the mix of underwriting, investments, taxes and share count matters.
